passages.t: ‘Let the rivers clap their hands’: a victory song for the King
passages.happening:
The heading is one word: “A Psalm” (verse 1). Then: “Sing to the LORD a new song, for He has done wonders; His right hand and holy arm have gained Him the victory” (verse 1).

The victory is for all to see. “The LORD has proclaimed His salvation and revealed His righteousness to the nations” (verse 2). He has kept his promise to Israel, and “all the ends of the earth have seen the salvation of our God” (verse 3).

So the whole earth is called to make music. “Make a joyful noise to the LORD, all the earth” (verse 4). Bring the lyre and harp, the trumpets and the ram's horn, and shout “before the LORD, the King” (verse 6).

Then nature joins in. The sea roars (verse 7). “Let the rivers clap their hands, let the mountains sing together for joy before the LORD, for He comes to judge the earth” (verses 8 to 9). “He will judge the world with righteousness and the peoples with equity” (verse 9).
passages.hearers:
Psalm 98 sounds a lot like Psalm 96. Both begin with ‘a new song’ and end with God coming to judge the earth. But Psalm 98 says why the song is new: God has won a victory.

The psalm never says what the victory was. The words ‘right hand’ and ‘holy arm’ recall the song Moses sang after the Red Sea. They also match Isaiah, who said, “The LORD has bared His holy arm in the sight of all the nations; all the ends of the earth will see the salvation of our God” (Isaiah 52:10). Many scholars think of the return from exile in Babylon. Others hear the exodus. The psalm leaves it open.

When an army came home from battle, the people met it with music and dancing. This is a victory song, but the winner is God, and the whole world is invited to the celebration.

Trumpets and the ram's horn sounded at feasts, and when a king was anointed (1 Kings 1:39). Here they sound for the LORD, ‘the King’ (verse 6).
passages.later:
When old Simeon held the baby Jesus in the temple, he said, “For my eyes have seen Your salvation, which You have prepared in the sight of all people” (Luke 2:30-31), close to verse 3.

At Jesus' birth the angel brought “good news of great joy that will be for all the people” (Luke 2:10). Jesus said that if his followers were silent, “the very stones will cry out” (Luke 19:40).
passages.asks:
What has God done that deserves a new song from you? Psalm 98 says joy should be loud sometimes, with instruments and shouting.

And let the picture of clapping rivers and singing mountains stay with you. The world around you is not dead matter. It is part of a creation waiting for its King. Praise him with it.
